chapter: Sideman years: J.J., Tyree Glenn, Sweets
title: Work and recordings after the Vanguard, 1957-58
summary: Brown reviews recordings and Elvin recalls gigs with Pepper Adams and Donald Byrd.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay so that takes up through that very historical recording, Live Village Vanguard. That brings us to November 1957. I know that date, that’s up here. Elvin Jones Sonny Rollins Live at Village Vanguard November 1957. What happens after that? Cause I have the Jones—“Keeping up with the Joneses” and this is not long after, this is March of ‘58. As a matter of fact I bought it March 24th of this year. So did you make any other recordings other than the Vanguard recording, which you didn’t know was going to be a recording when you were up there, and up until this one? Was there a period when you were playing with other folks?
Well I don’t recall doing any. I know I played with other people cause Pepper Adams was in town, Donald Byrd and all these guys. They’d get a gig and call me up. It was like that.
So the folks from Detroit, you guys kept in touch?
Well you made a recording with Kenny Burrell so that would have been a little earlier. You also made a recording with Pepper Adams too, so it was about this time I guess.
